metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to patches/contributions submitted to the QEMU project; does not apply to other AI uses (API research, static analysis, debugging) whose output is not included in the contribution.

evidence.quote: Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content.

the "Signed-off-by" label in a patch submission is a statement that the author takes responsibility for the entire contents of the patch, including any parts that were generated or assisted by AI tools

domains.reasoning: The document explicitly bans AI-generated/assisted content in patch submissions, states this covers well-known LLM tools, and assigns responsibility for the entire patch (including AI-assisted parts) to the signing contributor via the Signed-off-by mechanism. Both supervision level and accountability holder are named, so this is fully addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for meeting/notetaker bots
domains.reasoning: The document is entirely about patch/code provenance and contribution certification; it never mentions meetings, recordings, or notetaker bots.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule naming documentation, blogs, or design assets specifically
domains.reasoning: The AI policy is framed entirely around 'contributions'/'patches' in the code-provenance sense (git commits, Signed-off-by). It never names documentation, blog posts, or design assets as a distinct category, so this domain is not addressed even though such content could arguably fall under 'contributions' in practice.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for AI in moderation
domains.reasoning: No text in the document discusses moderation actions (e.g., closing issues, banning users) by AI or otherwise.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on whether reviewers may use AI to review patches
domains.reasoning: The document describes human review tags (Reviewed-by, Acked-by, Tested-by) but never states whether AI tools may be used by reviewers or maintainers to perform review, nor any supervision level for that activity.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Limited to agentic tools whose generated code/content is included in a contribution to QEMU.

evidence.quote: Examples of tools impacted by this policy includes GitHub's CoPilot, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Meta's Code Llama, and code/content generation agents which are built on top of such tools.

domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly names 'code/content generation agents which are built on top of such tools' as covered by the same ban applied to LLM tools, and the same Signed-off-by accountability clause applies to their output. This is a narrow but named treatment of agentic/autonomous tool use in the contribution context.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule or rationale on energy/water/carbon impact of AI
domains.reasoning: The document's stated rationale for banning AI content is entirely about copyright/licensing/DCO compliance risk; no mention of energy, water, or hardware carbon footprint appears anywhere.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule or rationale on server/infrastructure strain from AI
domains.reasoning: No text discusses server load, CI capacity, or hardware financing/costs related to AI tool usage.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Where the training material is known, it is common for it to include large volumes of material under restrictive licensing/copyright terms.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule governing use of platform/user data for training
domains.reasoning: The document discusses the licensing/copyright uncertainty of AI training material only as a justification for banning AI-generated contributions; it sets no rule about training data use itself, e.g. whether QEMU project data may be used to train models.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The document, QEMU's code-provenance policy, imposes a firm, specifically-scoped ban on AI-generated or AI-assisted content (including agentic tools) in patch contributions and pins accountability to the submitting contributor via Signed-off-by, but it is silent on every other domain (notetaker bots, general content, moderation, AI-assisted review, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training-data use), with copyright/licensing risk of training data cited only as rationale for the contribution ban rather than as a rule in its own right.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
